heading: Direct vs. Regular Mutual Funds: SEBI's New Default Plan Rule Explained
tldr: From November 1, 2026, SEBI has mandated that direct mutual fund plans be the default option on Asset Management Companies' (AMCs) digital platforms.
This means when you invest in mutual funds online via an AMC, the direct plan will be pre-selected, promoting cost-efficiency.
Should you choose a regular plan, AMCs are now required to explicitly inform you about its comparatively higher expense ratio.
The key distinction between direct and regular plans lies in the expense ratio, with direct plans being cheaper as they exclude distributor commissions.
This regulatory change aims to increase transparency and empower investors to make more informed decisions about their mutual fund investments.
caption:
Big news if you invest in mutual funds online! From November 2026, when you buy funds directly from a company's website, the cheaper "direct" option will be automatically chosen for you. If you pick the slightly more expensive "regular" plan, they'll clearly tell you why it costs more. This change helps you keep more of your money working for you.
